title: Preterm labour and PPROM: corticosteroids, tocolysis and neuroprotection
subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
setting: Labour room, antenatal ward, referral unit
summary: If birth is likely within 7 days at 24 to 34 weeks and dating is reliable, give dexamethasone 6 mg IM 12-hourly x4. Use nifedipine tocolysis (24 to 33+6 weeks) only to complete steroids or allow transfer, magnesium sulphate before 32 weeks, erythromycin for PPROM and intrapartum GBS prophylaxis.

sections.title: Recognise and assess
items: Preterm labour: regular contractions (at least 6 per hour) with cervical change (dilated 3 cm or more, or 75% or more effaced) before 37+0 weeks. WHO uses this, PPROM, or a planned preterm birth to define a high likelihood of birth within 7 days.
Establish gestational age as accurately as possible (first-trimester ultrasound is best). Steroid benefit depends on reliable dating.
PPROM: history of fluid leak with pooling of liquor on sterile speculum examination. Avoid digital vaginal examination in PPROM unless in active labour (infection risk).

Look for causes and contraindications to delaying birth: chorioamnionitis (maternal fever, maternal or fetal tachycardia, uterine tenderness, offensive liquor), abruption or bleeding, pre-eclampsia, urinary infection, fetal compromise.

sections.title: Investigations
items: CBC, urine microscopy and culture, low vaginal and rectal swab for group B streptococcus where available; blood cultures if febrile.
Ultrasound for presentation, estimated fetal weight, liquor volume and placental site; fetal heart monitoring or CTG.
Where available, transvaginal cervical length or fetal fibronectin helps decide who is truly in preterm labour when membranes are intact.

sections.title: Antenatal corticosteroids (WHO 2022)
items: Give from 24+0 to 34+0 weeks when ALL are met: reliable gestational age, high likelihood of birth within 7 days, no clinical evidence of maternal infection, adequate childbirth care, and newborn care available (resuscitation, thermal care, kangaroo mother care, feeding support, infection treatment, CPAP).

Dexamethasone 6 mg IM every 12 hours for 4 doses (preferred: cheaper and on the Essential Medicines List), or betamethasone 12 mg IM every 24 hours for 2 doses. Start even if the full course may not be completed before birth.

Indicated in singleton or multiple pregnancy, PPROM without infection, hypertensive disorders, fetal growth restriction, and pre-gestational or gestational diabetes (monitor glucose closely for 72 hours and adjust insulin).
Do not give with chorioamnionitis, or for planned caesarean at 34+0 to 36+6 weeks.
One repeat course only if the first course was at least 7 days earlier and birth is again likely within 7 days.

sections.title: Tocolysis (WHO 2022)
items: Purpose: delay birth by about 48 hours to complete steroids or to transfer the mother to a unit with neonatal care. Tocolysis alone does not reduce perinatal mortality.
Nifedipine is the only recommended tocolytic: spontaneous preterm labour, accurately dated 24+0 to 33+6 weeks, no contraindication to tocolysis.
Nifedipine immediate-release 20 mg orally, then 10 mg every 6 hours for 3 to 7 days or until transfer is complete, whichever comes first. Monitor maternal pulse and BP and the fetal heart.
Do not use tocolysis with vaginal bleeding or abruption, intrauterine infection, fetal death or lethal anomaly, fetal compromise, or maternal haemodynamic instability.
Use one agent only. Avoid betamimetics (serious maternal adverse effects). COX inhibitors (indometacin) only before 28 weeks and never in the third trimester (ductal constriction, oligohydramnios).
Nifedipine with magnesium sulphate may add to hypotension; monitor BP when both are running.

sections.title: Magnesium sulphate for fetal neuroprotection
items: Give to women with imminent preterm birth (expected within 24 hours) before 32+0 weeks to reduce cerebral palsy; singleton or multiple pregnancy (WHO 2015).
Regimen: 4 g IV over 20 minutes, then 1 g/h until birth or for 24 hours, whichever comes first. WHO found no evidence favouring one tested regimen; trials also used a single 4 g IV dose.
Monitor as for pre-eclampsia: respiratory rate, patellar reflexes, urine output; calcium gluconate 10% 10 mL IV slowly for toxicity.
It is not a tocolytic. Do not delay an urgent birth to give it.

sections.title: Antibiotics: PPROM and GBS prophylaxis
items: PPROM: erythromycin 250 mg orally 6-hourly for 10 days or until birth (WHO 2015, ORACLE I regimen). If unavailable, use a penicillin such as amoxicillin. Do not use co-amoxiclav (necrotising enterocolitis in the newborn).
Preterm labour with intact membranes and no signs of infection: no routine antibiotics apart from intrapartum GBS prophylaxis.

Intrapartum GBS prophylaxis in preterm labour or PPROM when GBS status is positive or unknown (routine screening is not done in most Indian units): benzylpenicillin 5 million units (3 g) IV, then 2.5 to 3 million units (1.5 g) IV every 4 hours until birth; or ampicillin 2 g IV, then 1 g IV every 4 hours.

Penicillin allergy at low anaphylaxis risk: cefazolin 2 g IV, then 1 g every 8 hours. High risk: clindamycin 900 mg IV every 8 hours if the isolate is susceptible, otherwise vancomycin 20 mg/kg IV every 8 hours (maximum 2 g per dose).
Suspected chorioamnionitis: broad-spectrum IV antibiotics per local protocol, no tocolysis, and expedite birth.

sections.title: Place and mode of birth
items: Transfer in utero to a centre with a neonatal unit, especially before 34 weeks, if birth is not imminent and the mother is stable.
Caesarean section is not routinely recommended to improve preterm newborn outcomes, whether cephalic or breech (WHO 2015); decide on obstetric grounds.
Have a neonatal team present. Do not clamp the cord before 1 minute in a baby who does not need resuscitation; start thermal care and kangaroo mother care early.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Giving corticosteroids when dating is uncertain, when birth is not likely within 7 days, or routinely after 34 weeks; in low-resource settings this has caused harm (ACT trial).
Tocolysis with suspected chorioamnionitis or abruption, or beyond 34 weeks.
Repeated digital vaginal examinations in PPROM.
Co-amoxiclav for PPROM.
Sublingual or bitten nifedipine, or combining tocolytics.

drugs.name: Dexamethasone
drugs.dose: 6 mg IM every 12 hours for 4 doses (total 24 mg)
drugs.notes: 24+0 to 34+0 weeks when WHO conditions are met. One repeat course only after at least 7 days.

drugs.name: Betamethasone
drugs.dose: 12 mg IM every 24 hours for 2 doses

drugs.name: Nifedipine immediate-release (tocolysis)
drugs.dose: 20 mg orally, then 10 mg every 6 hours for 3 to 7 days or until transfer
drugs.notes: 24+0 to 33+6 weeks. Monitor BP; avoid with hypotension or cardiac disease.

drugs.name: Magnesium sulphate (neuroprotection)
drugs.dose: 4 g IV over 20 minutes, then 1 g/h until birth or for 24 hours
drugs.notes: Before 32+0 weeks when birth is expected within 24 hours.

drugs.name: Erythromycin
drugs.dose: 250 mg orally every 6 hours for 10 days or until birth

drugs.name: Benzylpenicillin (penicillin G)
drugs.dose: 5 million units (3 g) IV, then 2.5 to 3 million units (1.5 g) IV every 4 hours until birth

drugs.name: Ampicillin
drugs.dose: 2 g IV, then 1 g IV every 4 hours until birth

drugs.name: Cefazolin
drugs.dose: 2 g IV, then 1 g IV every 8 hours until birth
drugs.notes: GBS prophylaxis with penicillin allergy at low anaphylaxis risk.
